title: Open problem: Does a sequence model trained on a source of exactly known entropy rate reach that entropy
statement: Does a sequence model trained on a source of exactly known entropy rate reach that entropy rate as parameters and tokens grow, or settle above it, and is any excess a property of the architecture class rather than of the source? STATED ON THE POSING PAPERS' OWN TERMS. The one-layer case is CLOSED and the open part is the depth and scale generalisation, which Makkuva et al. pose themselves. Their Theorem 1 gives the global minimum as "L(theta*) = H(x_{n+1}\|x_n), the entropy rate of the Markov chain"; their Figure 2a shows the test loss converging to it; the plateau they report appears only under weight tying and "Increasing the depth, however, solves the issue". COMPUTABLE PART, and it is the tractable leg: for small exact-H sources (finite-order Markov chains and probabilistic finite-state automata, H exact by dynamic programming) measure the finite-scale gap KL = H(p,q) - H(p) over a parameter/token ladder for a transformer and for a gated-linear-recurrent/SSM family, and report a fitted asymptote WITH AN INTERVAL against H, plus the interval's sensitivity to the fit form. NOT-COMPUTABLE PART: the theoretical characterisation at higher depths that Makkuva et al. name. TWO WARNINGS, both from documents already opened, which exist so this row is not re-derived from scratch. (1) THE NAIVE FIT IS KNOWN TO FAIL ON THIS FAMILY: Pandey (arXiv:2405.16684) fits exactly the estimator E + A/N^alpha + B/D^beta on five PCFG datasets, N from 4.2M to 1.4B and D from 100K to 100M, and prints E = -0.734, -0.262, -1.446, -1693.171, 1.174 in its Table 2 - and a cross-entropy floor cannot be negative, so the estimator must be re-specified or constrained before any asymptote is claimed. (2) THE FINITE-SCALE QUANTITY IS ALREADY MEASURED and must not be re-presented as new: Borenstein et al. (arXiv:2406.04289) compute it over 2100 random PFSAs for an LSTM and a GPT-2-style transformer. A context length must be declared, because at fixed context even a perfect predictor has floor H_T - H > 0 on a source with memory, and for an ambiguous PCFG the closed-form entropy rule is wrong (H(D) = H(S) + H(D\|S)), so declare the grammar unambiguous or compute H by inside-outside.

inputs.source_showing_it_is_open: Makkuva, Bondaschi, Girish, Nagle, Jaggi, Kim & Gastpar, "Attention with Markov", arXiv:2402.04161, read at section level by one reader on one route (LATEGATE4-07-2): "Theoretically characterizing this phenomenon for higher depths is an interesting open direction". The measurement leg's own gap is declared by Borenstein, Svete, Chan, Valvoda, Nowak, Gastpar, Cotterell & DuSell, arXiv:2406.04289, in its own limitations - "Our experiments also omit the effect of training dataset size" - and by Henighan et al., arXiv:2010.14701, which defines the limit and concedes "we cannot yet obtain a meaningful estimate for the entropy of natural language". No source any of five readers opened prints a fitted asymptote with an interval against an analytic H.
inputs.tier: A for the finite-scale measurement leg (exact H by dynamic programming, models small enough to train without a cluster); B for the asymptote-with-interval leg, which needs a ladder and a re-specified estimator; B for the theoretical characterisation Makkuva et al. name
inputs.how: Work it as PROMPT.md describes. Open the source first and confirm the problem is still open. State exactly what you established and what you did not.
